headline_hook: GPT-5.6 Closes a 30-Year Math Gap While Stack Overflow Falls Off a Cliff

pick_of_the_day.thesis: Closing a 30-year-old gap in convex optimization isn't impressive because a model did math — it's impressive because it suggests frontier LLMs are now generating novel mathematical objects that human researchers can verify but hadn't discovered, fundamentally changing the researcher-tool relationship.

model_literacy.relevance: GPT-5.6's convex optimization result crosses the line from AI-as-calculator (verifying or reproducing known proofs) to AI-as-collaborator (proposing novel constructions humans hadn't found). Understanding this distinction helps builders evaluate which 'AI does math' claims represent genuine capability advances.

items.title: GPT-5.6 Bridges a 30-Year Gap in Convex Optimization
items.angle: Not a benchmark flex — a frontier model producing a novel mathematical construction that closes an open problem. This is AI contributing to unsolved research, not reproducing textbook answers.
items.key_fact: 30-year gap in convex optimization theory reportedly closed via a prompt-driven approach
